$comment: OMN-18629. THE BASELINE. Occurrences that existed when the governed-helper
gate landed. Read by scripts/ci/governed_helper_gate.py.
THIS IS A RATCHET, NOT AN ALLOWLIST, and two properties enforce that.
(1) Every entry cites the ticket that will REMOVE it. An entry whose
'ticket' is missing or empty is a load-time refusal, so growing this file
without filing the work is unavailable. The three sweeps are OMN-18630
(locks), OMN-18631 (consumer commits) and OMN-18632 (interpreter
invocations). The three scripts/lane-census-check.sh entries this file carried

when it was first generated are GONE: omnibase_infra#3717 landed the OMN-18606 fix while this gate was being built, and the STALE check caught the drift in CI within the hour. That is the rule working, not an inconvenience.
(2) An entry the scanner NO LONGER MATCHES fails the gate as STALE. A fixed
call site may not leave cover behind for the next one at the same path, so
deleting the entry is part of fixing the occurrence. This file may shrink
and may never widen.
Keyed on (pair, path, digest-of-the-matched-line) with an occurrence count,
not on line numbers: an unrelated edit above a baselined call site must not
un-baseline it, or the gate fires on work that touched nothing it governs.
The COUNT is what stops a second identical call site in an already-listed
file from riding in on the first one's entry.
Every entry also carries a verdict -- defect, benign, not-a-call-site or dead --
and the reason, judged from the call site and not from the pattern. The loader
refuses an entry without both. The gate run with --base-ref refuses any entry
the base ref does not carry or whose count is above the base ref's, which is
what makes 'may shrink and may never widen' true of a ticket-citing entry too.
'note' is the matched line, for a reader. It is not read by the checker and
carries no authority: the digest is the key.

The commit() method has no caller; HandlerDlqReplay uses commit_offsets (OMN-17896) and the docstring says the method is only retained.

aiokafka commits the position of records yielded to the caller; every record getmany returned is in the batch being flushed, so the commit never passes an unflushed record. A failed flush is counted and dropped, so the next commit covers it.
aiokafka async-for yields one record at a time, so the argument-less commit covers exactly the record just handled; the second site commits a failed record on purpose (poison pill).
aiokafka async-for yields one record at a time, so the argument-less commit covers exactly the record just handled; the skip and validation-error sites commit a rejected record on purpose.
A test fixture that reads one record with getmany(max_records=1) and commits so the consumer group holds an offset; no record is left unhandled.
The fallback taken when flock is absent: a bare mkdir lock released only by an rmdir and an EXIT trap, with no holder record, so a SIGKILL leaves a lock nobody can tell from a live one.
Creates the directory that will hold the lock files, not a lock.
The fallback taken when flock is absent: a bare mkdir lock polled forever with no holder record and released only by an EXIT trap, so a SIGKILL leaves every later run waiting on a corpse.

Writes the owner PID into the lock and, by design, refuses to reclaim it: a second deployer exits 2 naming the recorded PID. It records no host or timestamp, but it fails loudly rather than reporting a held lock as nothing to do.

Writes pid, host and timestamp into the lock directory and reclaims it only when that pid is gone on the same host: the holder protocol, which the pattern cannot see because the record is written on the next line.
